brief.ask: Set the art direction for 12 kids' evites starring Plajah's own kaiju mascots, Chora (music note on the belly, purple goggle markings) and Reello (camera, orange goggle markings). Decide the 12 scenarios, how the mascots perform inside the invite (they can be animated 2D puppets or the rigged 3D models), and how a guest's tap or game makes them react.
brief.audience: Kids and parents; also brand-building for Plajah itself.
brief.feeling: Our characters, our world: mischievous, warm, unmistakably Plajah.
constraints: Surface: Plajah Evites, an invitation opened on a phone browser by guests who never sign up; also shared as a link preview and QR.

Build method (fixed): each design is a layered Tela document: a generated art plate, separate transparent foreground cut-outs that drift and react to phone tilt, a WebGL effects layer (foil shimmer, light leaks, bokeh, particles, candle flicker) revealed through masks, and live text in Tela. Names, dates and venues are never baked into the art.
Bar: consumer-facing, jaw-dropping, high-end professional. Must stay legible at 390px wide, honour reduced motion, and load fast on mobile data.
No copyrighted characters; kids art is original or Plajah-owned.

Production is GENERATIVE ONLY (Magnific image models, shaders, procedural code, renders of Plajah-owned 3D assets). One Magnific draft grid returns 8 to 16 distinct plates for a flat cost, so a whole collection can be explored in one or two prompts: direct those prompts.
The mascots must stay on-model (wide mochi head, white face, chevron cap with navy gem, goggle patches, angular magenta/orange ruff, cat-ear horns).
references: Exploration grid A: Chora and Reello at a birthday party, one holding a frosted cake with candles, the other with a party horn, balloons and string lights, confetti; on-model, polished 3D.
Exploration grid B: the two dancing on a light-up disco floor under a mirror ball; on-model, energetic.

proposals.title: The Measure Holds, They Play
proposals.idea: Each evite is a single governed composition — one motivated light source, one axis of symmetry, one typographic cantus firmus — inside which Chora and Reello perform with controlled mischief, so the card reads instantly on first glance and rewards every tap afterward.
proposals.geometry: A strict 3:4 portrait proportion (390×520px safe zone) anchored by a central vertical axis and a golden-section horizon line at roughly 62% from top. The mascots are always placed in dialogue across that axis — never both left, never floating without a responding element. Twelve scenarios are organized as four trios: Celebration (birthday, dance, parade, confetti-storm), Nature (underwater, forest, night-sky, rain), Making (music studio, photography darkroom, cooking, building), and Portal (door to another world, rising curtain, rocket launch, paper-fold reveal) — four trios yielding twelve scenes. Each scene inherits the same underlying grid: a ruled upper register for live Tela event text, a dominant picture field at center-mass, a grounded lower band for RSVP action. The grid never breaks; only the characters inside it move.
proposals.typography: Cantus firmus headline: Playfair Display SC (OFL, Google Fonts) — small-caps, tracked at +60, set at a scale that fills exactly one-quarter of the card width per cap, so the word 'PARTY' or 'SHOW' becomes a structural beam. Supporting text: Jost Regular (OFL, Google Fonts), 13–15px, sentence case, 1.5 line-height — subordinate, never competing. The two faces create the hierarchy Brunelleschi gave the Pazzi Chapel: dominant order above, quiet function below. Date and venue arrive in Jost Medium, same size as body, distinguished only by a foil-shimmer WebGL tint on the numeral cluster — no size inflation, no screaming caps.
proposals.imageLogic: No photography. Every plate is a Magnific generative render directed as follows — Prompt A (Celebration trio): 'Chora and Reello, wide mochi heads, white faces, chevron cap navy gem, purple and orange goggle patches, angular magenta-orange ruff, cat-ear horns — on-model; Chora holds a six-tier frosted cake with lit candles, Reello blows a paper horn; background: warm liminal banquet hall, single overhead motivated spotlight casting one unified shadow beneath both characters, volumetric confetti in slow fall; 3D render, subsurface-scatter skin, physically-based lighting, 8 variants in one grid, landscape orientation for cropping.' Prompt B (Nature trio): same character spec, swap setting to bioluminescent tide pool / moonlit forest clearing / rain-slicked city roof — single cool-key light from upper left in all three, maintaining cross-scene light grammar. The eight-to-sixteen plate grid
proposals.texture: Simulated: the background plate carries a subtle paper-grain overlay (procedural shader, grain size 0.4px at 390px, opacity 8%) that reads as a high-quality printed card stock. The foreground mascot layer has a micro-specular pass baked into the Magnific render — the goggle lenses catch the single light source as a hard catchlight, reinforcing the unified light grammar. No physical scan, no photograph of texture; the grain is procedurally generated at render time and remains consistent across all twelve scenes because it is driven by the same noise seed. The foil-shimmer WebGL layer is masked to the goggle lenses, the navy gem on the cap, and the numeral cluster in the date — three fixed mask regions that never change, giving the shimmer structural purpose rather than decoration.
proposals.motion: Entrance: the background plate fades in over 400ms (ease-in-out cubic); the mascot foreground layer drops 12px and rises to position over 600ms with a weighted-escapement easing curve (fast start, slow settle — referencing the governed arc of a tower-clock escapement, not a rubber bounce). The cantus-firmus headline types on character by character at 40ms intervals after the mascot lands — 600ms total — so the text arrives as consequence of the characters, not ahead of them. Idle: Chora and Reello breathe with a 3.2-second sinusoidal vertical drift of ±4px, out of phase by exactly half a cycle — they never rise together, so the axis of symmetry pulses rather than nods. Tap interaction: a tap on either mascot triggers a 200ms anticipation squash (scale Y 0.92), then a 280ms pop to scale 1.08, then a 400ms return — the character reacts to being touched without abandoning its ground plane.
proposals.productionMethod: Two Magnific prompt calls: Call 1 covers the Celebration and Nature trios (six scenes, 8-variant grid each = up to 16 plates per call, select best six plus two alternates). Call 2 covers Making and Portal trios. Selected plates are imported to Tela as locked background layers. Foreground mascot cut-outs are extracted via Tela's generative mask tool from the same Magnific render — no separate asset needed. WebGL foil shader is written once as a Tela effect module, parameterized by (lightVectorX, lightVectorY) inherited from each plate's established light direction — the same constraint system across all twelve cards. Typography is live Tela text; names, dates, venues are never baked. The procedural paper-grain shader is a single GLSL snippet shared across all twelve. Total generative cost: two Magnific grid calls plus one shader authored once.
proposals.humanTrace: The light vector in every WebGL foil effect is not computed — it is read by eye from the Magnific render and entered as a directed angle by the art director. That act of looking at where the light falls and encoding it as a governing parameter is the compositional judgment that organizes the entire system. The editorial selection of which plate from the 8–16-variant grid becomes the canonical scene is a second act of judgment. The easing curve on the mascot entrance — the weighted-escapement deceleration — is specified in cubic-bezier values chosen to feel governed rather than springy, and that specification is a performance decision, not an algorithm's output.
proposals.risk: The risk is that structural gravity reads as stiffness to children, who expect chaos. The counter-argument is Fantasia: Disney's most formally organized animated film is also one of the most beloved by children precisely because the structure gives the surprises somewhere to land. Chora and Reello's mischief is funnier inside a composed frame than against visual noise — the held measure makes the joke. The secondary risk is that Playfair Display SC reads as adult; this is mitigated by its large scale and the characters' own warmth carrying the register.

arguesWith.why: The Baroque Dramatist will want the reveal to announce itself — a radial burst, a curtain sweep, a crescendo of particle effects that builds to the mascots' entrance. I reject this on structural grounds: if the effect announces the reveal, the reveal has already happened and the characters arrive into a room that has been decorated without them. proposals.title: Ink-Run Kaiju Party Press
proposals.idea: Each evite is a bootleg concert poster — Chora and Reello silkscreen-printed (generatively simulated) onto a misregistered ground, so the characters feel pulled off a wall rather than rendered in a studio, and every tap or tilt smears the ink one deliberate step further.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 9:19.5 mobile bleed. Background is a two-color simulated Risograph plate: one color floods the top two-thirds (the scene), one color floods the bottom third (the info block). The two plates are offset by 4–8px horizontally — visible misregistration, not accidental. Mascots occupy a centered vertical axis, heads breaking the plate boundary at the top. Info block sits on a ruled baseline grid of 4 rows: event type / name field / date+time field / venue field. No decorative border; the plate edge IS the border, rough and slightly bowed as if the paper buckled under heat.
proposals.typography: Headlines: Space Grotesk Bold (Google Fonts / OFL), all-caps, tracked +80, set at 11vw — big enough to read as a poster slogan, not a card sentiment. Secondary info: Space Grotesk Regular, 14px / 20px leading, same tracking as body copy on a zine. Party-type label (BIRTHDAY / SLEEPOVER / etc.): Boogaloo (Google Fonts / OFL), 9vw, sentence case, positioned top-left corner like a venue stamp. No script faces — script is warmth through decoration; warmth here comes from the ink, not the letterform.
proposals.imageLogic: Magnific generative grid directed to produce 12 distinct Risograph-style plates: two ink colors per plate, halftone dot grain visible at 50% zoom, slight ink spread at character edges, each plate cropped to show Chora and/or Reello in a specific scenario (see 12 scenarios in productionMethod). Characters generated on-model using Plajah 3D rig renders as reference input, then style-transferred into the Risograph simulation so the mochi head, chevron cap, goggle patches, and angular ruff all survive the grain. No photographic source material from outside Plajah assets. The 8–16 plate return from one prompt batch covers the full 12-card set with alternates.
proposals.texture: Simulated Risograph: visible halftone rosette at 45° angle, ink-spread halo 2–3px around character silhouettes, paper tooth simulated via a procedural noise layer (Perlin, low frequency, 8% opacity) baked into the art plate. The misregistration offset is hardcoded into the Tela layer stack — plate A (scene color) and plate B (shadow/second color) are separate transparent PNGs, so the offset can be tuned per card without regenerating art. WebGL foil shimmer is masked ONLY to the mascots' goggle patches and the gem on the chevron cap — nowhere else. Foil does not smooth the halftone; it sits over it, proving the grain existed before the sheen.
proposals.motion: On load: plate B (shadow layer) slides in 6px from its misregistered position over 0.4s ease-out, as if the second ink pass just landed — this is the only entrance animation and it plays once. On phone tilt (gyroscope): foreground mascot cut-out drifts ±12px on X and Y at 60fps, parallax depth 1.2× relative to background plate — the drift feels like the poster is laminated behind glass and the character is pressed to the front surface. On tap: a procedural ink-splat particle burst (WebGL, 8–12 droplets, 0.3s, color matches plate A) fires from the tap point and fades; the mascot's arm or tail snaps to a second pose via a 2-frame 2D puppet cut (no tweening — it cuts, like a risograph can only be one state at a time). Reduced motion: tilt parallax and tap burst are disabled; the load animation collapses to a simple opacity fade; poster reads as a static image with no loss of meaning.
proposals.productionMethod: Step 1 — Magnific prompt batch (one prompt, 12–16 outputs): 'Risograph two-color poster illustration, [scenario], Chora and Reello kaiju characters — wide mochi head, white face, chevron cap with navy gem, purple goggle patches (Chora) / orange goggle patches (Reello), angular magenta-orange ruff, cat-ear horns — halftone dot grain, ink spread at edges, misregistered second color plate offset 6px right, flat graphic shapes, no gradients, no photorealism, poster crop, portrait 9:19 ratio.' Scenarios directed per card: 01 Birthday cake + candles, 02 Disco floor mirror ball, 03 Sleepover pillow fort, 04 Backyard movie night, 05 Science fair explosion, 06 Pool party splash, 07 Costume parade, 08 Karaoke stage, 09 Camping s'mores, 10 Art studio paint fight, 11 Skate park ramp, 12 Stargazing rooftop. Step 2 — Editorial selection: pick one hero plate per scenario from the batch; reject any outp
proposals.humanTrace: The misregistration offset — that 4–8px slip between plate A and plate B — is a committed editorial decision, not a random jitter. It is set once per card, logged in the Tela layer stack as a named offset value, and it does not drift or animate. It is the record of a choice about where the second ink pass landed, the way a printer decides how much slip is expressive versus broken. The halftone rosette angle (45°) is also a decision: 45° is the traditional angle for black plates in offset lithography, applied here to the scene color because the scene is the 'black' — the information — and the party color is the 'spot.' Those two decisions, offset and angle, are the marks I can defend.
proposals.risk: Kids' party invitations are expected to be soft, round, gradient-smooth and legible-from-across-a-room cheerful. This direction is rough at the edges, typographically blunt, and structurally confrontational — it looks like something torn off a telephone pole, not something a parent receives and feels reassured by. The risk is that parents read 'bootleg poster' as 'low production value' before they read it as 'intentional character.' That risk is worth taking because Plajah's stated identity is mischievous and unmistakably itself — and a Risograph kaiju poster IS mischievous and unmistakably itself in a way that a gradient bubble card never will be. The tap-ink-splat interaction is also a risk: it is abrupt and non-reversible within the session, which is the point — it is a mark, not a toggle — but a child who taps repeatedly gets a screen covered in splats, and that is either a delight o

arguesWith.why: The Baroque Dramatist will want to fill the info block with layered ornament, candle-flicker gradients, and a full chromatic party of particle effects across the whole surface. I am holding the WebGL foil to the goggle patches and the gem only, and the ink splat fires once per tap at a single point. The Dramatist reads this as withholding. proposals.title: State Machines in Mochi Skin
proposals.idea: Each evite is a small physics engine wearing Chora and Reello as its interface — the mascots are not illustrations posed in a scene but live input-output nodes whose body states (ear droop, goggle glow intensity, ruff oscillation frequency, cap gem pulse rate) are direct functions of measurable guest interaction: tap count, tilt angle, hold duration, and ambient light level read from the device.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 390×844px canvas divided into three horizontal bands by a strict 12-column, 8-row modular grid: Band 1 (rows 1–3) is the generative art plate — a deep-field environment rendered with physically-based lighting from a single motivated source whose direction propagates as a constraint into every downstream layer; Band 2 (rows 4–6) is the mascot puppet stage — Chora and Reello occupy left and right thirds of a shared ground plane, centre third reserved for the interaction affordance (tap target, tilt axis indicator, or game HUD); Band 3 (rows 7–8) is live Tela text, never baked, always legible at 14px minimum. Foreground cut-out layers drift on gyro tilt along a parallax z-stack of exactly four depth planes (0.0, 0.4, 0.8, 1.2 rem shift per degree), maintaining dimensional coherence with the art plate's light source direction so highlights never contradict shadows.
proposals.typography: Space Grotesk (Google Fonts / OFL) for all display headings — its geometric skeleton reads as system-native without feeling cold; numerals have the mechanical confidence of instrument panels. Body and detail text in DM Mono, also OFL, because dates, times and venue strings are data, and monospace treats them honestly. Scale: heading 28px / 1.1 leading, subhead 18px / 1.3, body 14px / 1.5. All caps suppressed except for the single-word scenario label (BIRTHDAY · CONCERT · SLEEPOVER etc.) set in Space Grotesk 11px tracked at 0.18em — a system-status badge, not a shout. No decorative lettering; no hand-script fonts pretending to be warm.
proposals.imageLogic: No photography enters. The art plate is a Magnific generative render directed as a physically-based 3D scene: one prompt per scenario set of four, returning 8–16 plate variants per grid run. Prompt architecture specifies: motivated light source direction (angle in degrees from upper-left, elevation, colour temperature), environment geometry (volumetric fog density, floor material — prismatic acrylic, bioluminescent moss, mirror tile, etc.), and mascot silhouette positions as placeholder geometry so the plate's empty stage reads correctly at generation time. Mascots are never baked into the plate; they are rigged Plajah-owned 3D assets composited as separate transparent foreground layers, so on-model fidelity is guaranteed by the rig, not by prompt luck. WebGL layer applies foil shimmer as a normal-map-driven specular pass whose highlight direction is locked to the same azimuth as the pla
proposals.texture: Simulated prismatic foil on the art plate border and goggle patches — generated as a WebGL shader sampling a procedural rainbow LUT remapped by view angle and masked to the foil regions only. No plastic gloss on the mascot bodies; instead a subsurface-scatter approximation (thin SSS pass baked into the 3D render, not a post filter) gives the mochi skin its characteristic soft translucency without reading as latex. Ruff material is angular faceted fabric — anisotropic specular, direction aligned to the ruff's geometric segments. Particle systems (confetti, sparks, musical notes, bokeh) are GPU instanced, each particle a billboard with a procedurally varied alpha decay curve so no two confetti pieces share an identical fade — this is the system producing honest imperfection, not scanned noise.
proposals.motion: State machine with four named states per mascot, transitions governed by input events, not timers. IDLE: slow 0.8Hz breathing cycle, ear micro-oscillation ±2°, goggle glow at 40% intensity, ruff at rest frequency 0.3Hz. ALERT (first tap detected): ear erect in 80ms ease-out, goggle glow ramps to 100% in 120ms, ruff frequency jumps to 1.2Hz, Chora's music-note belly mark pulses once in sync with a haptic. REACT (tap held >400ms or tilt >15°): mascot leans into tilt direction along the parallax axis, ruff segments fan outward, particle system fires at rate proportional to tilt magnitude (0–60 particles/sec), cap gem strobes at 4Hz. CELEBRATE (interaction threshold met — varies by scenario, e.g. 5 taps, or tilt held 2s): full-body jump arc (Chora 120ms up, 180ms down with squash), Reello's camera-belly flashes a simulated shutter, confetti burst 200 particles, foil shimmer amplitude doubles
proposals.productionMethod: Two Magnific prompt grid runs: Run 1 targets birthday, concert, sleepover, and science-lab scenarios (4 scenarios × 4 variants = 16 plates); Run 2 targets beach, jungle, space, bakery, art-studio, sports-arena, haunted-house, and winter-forest (8 scenarios × 2 variants = 16 plates). Prompt structure per scenario: '[scenario environment], physically-based 3D render, single motivated light source at [azimuth]° [elevation]°, [colour temperature]K, volumetric atmosphere, prismatic floor material, empty centre stage for character compositing, no text, no watermark, aspect ratio 9:20'. Mascot renders: Plajah's existing rigged 3D assets rendered in Blender (GPL, zero additional cost) at matching light direction per scenario, exported as transparent PNG sprite sheets covering the four animation states. WebGL effects layer: custom GLSL shader, open source, written once and parameterised per scena
proposals.humanTrace: The motivated light source direction for each scenario is a human editorial decision made before the prompt is written — it is not left to the model. I specify the azimuth and elevation in degrees, then verify that the Blender mascot render and the WebGL foil shader both inherit that exact value. The selection pass (choosing which of 16 plates advances) is a human judgment call on dimensional coherence: does the shadow on the floor match the highlight on the ruff? Plates that fail this test are rejected regardless of how 'nice' they look. This is the trace: a physicist's insistence on consistency as the editorial eye, applied at generation time and again at compositing time.
proposals.risk: The interaction model is more demanding to implement than a static illustration — it requires a working state machine, a gyro API call, and a WebGL shader, all inside a Tela evite that must load fast on mobile data. The risk is that engineering constraints force simplification of the state machine, collapsing four states into two and losing the graduated response that makes the mascots feel alive rather than merely reactive. That risk is worth taking because a Plajah evite that demonstrates genuine input-output behaviour — where the child's tap measurably changes the character's state — is a product demonstration as well as an invitation. It proves the platform can do something a printed card or a static JPEG link preview cannot. The 'jaw-dropping' bar in the brief is not met by a pretty picture; it is met by a character that knows you tapped it.

arguesWith.why: The Baroque Dramatist will want a reveal sequence — a cinematic opening, a moment of maximum spectacle, a choreographed crescendo. I expect a proposal for a 3-second intro animation that plays once and then settles. proposals.title: Field Notes from Kaiju Country
proposals.idea: Each evite is a traveler's field-notebook page — torn margin, ink-bleed registration, stamped location seal — where Chora and Reello have physically arrived inside the document as generative 3D renders composited onto procedurally-aged paper, and every tap reveals a new annotation in their hand.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 390 × 780px. The page is divided by a ragged horizontal tear at roughly the golden ratio (≈480px from top): upper zone is the 'plate' — full-bleed generated scene; lower zone is the 'notes field' — ruled notebook lines at 28px leading, with a red margin rule at 48px from left, echoing Rhodia pad geometry. A stamped circular seal (48px diameter) sits at the intersection of tear and margin rule, functioning as the WebGL foil accent. Corner registration crosses at all four edges keep the composition tethered to a physical logic.
proposals.typography: Headline: Fraunces (OFL, Google Fonts) — variable optical-size axis cranked to 'small' for ink-trap drama at 48px, uppercase, tight −0.04em tracking; feels like a letterpress date-stamp. Body / party details: Inconsolata (OFL, Google Fonts) — monospace, 15px, normal weight, echoing typewriter field notes; live Tela text layer only, never baked. Accent annotations: Caveat (OFL, Google Fonts) — handwritten feel, 13px, used sparingly for Chora/Reello's in-world scrawls that appear on tap. All three are legible at 390px, all pass WCAG AA on the aged-paper background.
proposals.imageLogic: No photographs. All plates are Magnific generative renders directed as follows — Prompt A grid (8 plates, birthday scenarios): 'Chora and Reello, wide mochi heads, white faces, chevron caps with navy gems, goggle patches in purple and orange, angular magenta-orange ruffs, cat-ear horns, on-model, polished 3D render composited onto aged cream watercolor paper with visible deckle edge and ink-bleed halo, scene: [one of 8 birthday micro-scenarios], dramatic raking light from upper left, deep shadow bottom right, no background gradient, paper tooth visible in shadow areas, style: editorial children's book meets natural history illustration plate.' Prompt B grid (8 plates, adventure/non-birthday scenarios): same on-model spec, scenes include: stargazing rooftop, rainy-day reading fort, street-market snack stall, tide-pool expedition, night-market lantern walk, winter hot-chocolate kiosk, mids
proposals.texture: Procedural aged-paper shader in WebGL: cream base (#F5EED8) with grain noise at 0.4 opacity, subtle foxing spots, a faint blue-ruled line pattern at 28px, and a red margin line. The stamp seal uses the existing foil-shimmer WebGL mask — gold foil highlight direction locked to the single motivated upper-left light source established in the render, so the shimmer only activates on the raised-ink topography of the stamp geometry. Ink-bleed halo around the kaiju is a procedural edge-diffusion pass that reads the render's shadow boundary and softens it by 4–7px with a warm sepia tint, simulating ink soaking into paper tooth.
proposals.motion: Idle: Chora and Reello breathe (subtle 1.2s scale oscillation ±1.5% on the foreground layer, offset by 0.3s between characters). Phone tilt: the two foreground cut-outs parallax at different depths — Reello at 1× sensitivity, Chora at 0.7× — against the static plate, creating a shallow diorama. First tap anywhere: a Caveat-font annotation 'appears' as if written in real time (SVG path draw-on, 0.6s, sepia ink color) near the tapped character — a different scrawl per scenario (e.g., '🎂 you're invited!!' or '📷 Reello was HERE'). Second tap on the stamp seal: foil shimmer flares for 0.4s, bokeh particles (8–12 soft circles, warm gold) drift upward and fade over 1.8s. Candle-flicker particle is reserved for the birthday-cake scenarios only — small flame shader on the cake foreground cut-out, 24fps flicker, reduced-motion version replaces with a static warm glow. All motion respects prefers
proposals.productionMethod: Two Magnific prompt grids (A: 8 birthday plates, B: 8 adventure plates) generated in one session using the detailed on-model prompt above; editorial selection narrows to 12. Foreground kaiju cut-outs extracted via generative segmentation (no manual masking). Paper shader, foil mask, bokeh, and candle-flicker written as GLSL fragment shaders in Tela's WebGL layer, parameterized so the same shader stack serves all 12 evites with only the plate and cut-out swapped. Fraunces/Inconsolata/Caveat loaded via Google Fonts CDN. Names, dates, venues entered as live Tela text in the ruled notes field — never touching the art plate. Stamp seal is a procedural SVG with foil mask applied. Total generative cost: two flat-rate Magnific grids.
proposals.humanTrace: The ink-bleed halo is gated by the actual shadow boundary of each generated render — no two are identical. The foil shimmer on the stamp follows the same upper-left motivated light as the render's key light, so the luster is physically argued by the scene, not decorative. The Caveat annotations are unique per scenario, written by the art director as world-specific observations in Chora and Reello's voices, then encoded as SVG paths — they read as found notes, not UI copy.
proposals.risk: The notebook aesthetic could read as 'vintage travel brand' rather than 'kids party' if the warmth is not explicit in the kaiju staging and the Caveat annotations are not genuinely playful. The risk is worth it because it gives Plajah a visual identity that is not confetti-and-balloon generic — it positions the brand as a world with its own lore and geography, which is the long-term brand-building ask — and the field-notebook format makes the live-text 'notes field' feel native rather than slapped on.

arguesWith.why: The Dramatist will reach for full-bleed gold and saturated theatrical lighting across all 12 plates and call it 'world-building.' I will stop that direction: gold deployed without a physical argument — without the stamp's raised ink, without the single motivated light source — is decoration pretending to be meaning. proposals.title: Twelve Curtain Rises for Kaiju
proposals.idea: Each evite is a miniature opera house: a single breathtaking reveal built from chiaroscuro depth, physical-light simulation, and a tap-triggered moment where Chora or Reello tears through the picture plane itself — the guest is never a spectator, they pull the rope.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 9×16 stage, 390px wide. The frame is divided into three depth planes: a raked background plate (full bleed, slight perspective tilt, ~60% of height), a mid-stage cut-out layer where the mascots stand or float (transparent PNG, parallax on tilt), and a proscenium arch layer painted in light — a vignette that curves inward at the top corners like a theatre portal, masking the WebGL effects beneath it. The 12 scenarios are arranged as a 4×3 production grid internally, each with its own backstage vocabulary: a different light source position, a different mascot staging relationship (one in front, one behind; or both mid-leap; or one enormous and one tiny in false perspective), and a different particle event. Text lives in a safe zone occupying the lower 22% of the frame — never inside the picture plane, always below the proscenium lip.
proposals.typography: Headline: Fraunces (Google Fonts, OFL) — variable optical-size axis pushed to Display, weight 800, italic, sentence case, tracked loosely at +20. Fraunces has the ink-trap warmth of a 19th-century playbill without requiring a paid foundry. Sub-line and details: DM Sans (Google Fonts, OFL), weight 400, tight tracking, all-caps for date/time/venue fields, 13px floor for legibility. The headline letter-spacing breathes; the detail line is clipped and precise. No third face. On reduced-motion, all type is static and fully legible without animation context.
proposals.imageLogic: No photography. All plates are Magnific generative renders directed as follows — Prompt A (Birthday Opera): 'Chora and Reello, wide mochi heads, white faces, chevron caps with navy gem, orange and purple goggle patches, magenta-orange angular ruffs, cat-ear horns — rendered in high-gloss 3D, standing on a baroque theatrical stage strewn with frosted cake, candles, balloons, confetti; dramatic low-angle Rembrandt lighting from stage left, deep shadow behind, gold and warm amber practical lights, volumetric haze; the background is an opera-house curtain in deep crimson, partially torn open to reveal a starfield — 8 distinct scenarios in a single grid, each with a different emotional peak: blowing candles, mid-leap, holding cake aloft, arms wide in triumph, peering through a balloon cluster, pulling a party-popper, riding a confetti wave, frozen in a double-take — photorealistic material qu
proposals.texture: Simulated physical light is the primary texture: subsurface scattering on mochi skin (warm peachy undertone bleeding through highlights), foil shimmer on the angular ruffs (WebGL shader, angle-reactive), heavy film grain at 18% opacity (adds tactile 35mm weight without obscuring detail), volumetric haze in the mid-stage plane (a soft additive blur pass, particle-seeded), and wax-drip candle flicker on birthday plates (a looping 12-frame procedural shader, 0.8s cycle). The proscenium vignette has a slight paper-tooth edge — a procedural noise mask rather than a hard crop — so the frame feels hand-made rather than digital.
proposals.motion: The reveal is the event. Sequence on open: (1) black — 0.4s hold, building tension like a breath before a downbeat; (2) the background plate fades up from pure black, center-out, 0.6s ease-in — the stage is revealed before the actors; (3) the mascot cut-out layer rises from below the proscenium lip, 0.5s ease-out spring, as if the character walked on from the wings; (4) the WebGL layer ignites — foil shimmer pulses once, particles scatter, candle flames flicker into life — 0.3s burst then settle into idle loop. Idle state: mascots drift 4px on phone tilt (gyroscope parallax, mid-stage layer only), particles drift upward at 0.2px/frame, candles flicker continuously. Tap interaction: the tapped mascot breaks the fourth wall — they lean sharply toward camera (a 0.15s scale punch to 108%, then settle to 102%), their goggle patches brighten (WebGL emissive flash, 2 frames), and they emit a bu
proposals.productionMethod: Two Magnific prompt runs return 8–16 plates each (Prompt A: Birthday Opera 4×2 grid; Prompt B: Disco Revelation 4×2 grid; Prompt C if needed: 2–4 bonus scenarios). Art direction selects 12 plates. Each plate is processed: mascot silhouette separated as a transparent-background foreground layer (Magnific inpainting or generative background removal), background plate exported separately. Both assets import into Tela as layers. WebGL effects layer is a Tela-native shader stack (foil shimmer, bokeh, candle flicker, particle emitter) applied via mask tied to the proscenium vignette shape — a procedural vector drawn once and reused across all 12 templates. Fraunces and DM Sans load from Google Fonts CDN; text fields are live Tela variables (name, date, venue) never baked. Gyroscope parallax and tap interaction are Tela interaction triggers, not custom code. The entire collection is produced fr
proposals.humanTrace: The editorial hand is the trace: the decision of which of the 16 generated plates has the right light-source position for drama, which mascot staging relationship creates genuine tension, which particle event matches the emotional pitch of the scenario. Beyond selection, the proscenium vignette is hand-drawn as a procedural vector — its curve is a human decision, not a generated one. The film grain opacity and the candle-flicker timing (0.8s cycle, not 1.0s — because 1.0s feels metronomic and 0.8s feels alive) are performance choices. The 0.4s black hold at open is a dramaturgical decision: it is the moment before the curtain rises, and it is chosen, not computed.
proposals.risk: The baroque reveal sequence — black hold, stage-up, actor-enters, WebGL ignites — is four beats where a competitor would use one. On a slow mobile connection, those beats must land in under 2.5 seconds total or the drama collapses into a loading problem. The mitigation is aggressive asset compression (WebP plates, lazy-loaded WebGL layer) and a graceful degradation path where the static plate alone reads as a complete, beautiful invitation. The risk is worth it because the sequence is the product: a child who watches the curtain rise and then taps a kaiju into life has had an experience, not just read an invitation.

arguesWith.why: The Minimalist will argue that the four-beat open sequence is indulgent and that a single, well-chosen still frame communicates faster and more clearly. I reject this on grounds of emotional scale: speed of comprehension is not the measure of an invitation. An invitation is a promise of how the party will feel. proposals.title: One Silence, One Monster
proposals.idea: Each invite is a single held breath: maximum white void, one kaiju occupying exactly one third of the frame, and a single interaction that reveals the party detail hidden in the negative space around them.
proposals.geometry: 390px column. Vertical thirds: top third is pure void with live text floating at optical center — party detail only, no decoration. Middle third is the mascot, cropped asymmetrically so one goggle patch bleeds into the void above and the ruff bleeds into the void below — the body is the event horizon. Bottom third is void again, holding a single tap-target: a hairline circle, 32px, no label. The mascot's body is never centered; it sits 8px left of axis, creating a column of negative space on the right that carries the QR and link preview thumbnail. No background pattern. No confetti layer. No gradient. The ground the mascot stands on is implied by a single cast shadow, procedurally rendered, physically plausible.
proposals.typography: DM Sans (OFL, Google Fonts) for all live text. Party name: 28px, weight 300, tracked +80, all-caps, optical center of the void. Date and venue: 13px, weight 400, tracked +20, flush left, 24px from left edge. No decorative headline. No script. The type does not compete with the mascot — it occupies space the mascot refuses to fill.
proposals.imageLogic: No photographs. Each of the 12 art plates is a Magnific generative render: the mascot in a single, scenario-specific action pose against a pure white or near-white field, lit by one directional light source from upper left, casting one shadow. The shadow is the only texture in the scene. Prompt grid A (8 plates): Chora and Reello in eight distinct single-action moments — blowing a candle, catching a balloon string, mid-spin on an empty floor, holding a cake at arm's length, pressing a camera shutter, covering one goggle in mock-surprise, sitting cross-legged with a party horn untouched in their lap, and one plate of both mascots back-to-back looking in opposite directions. Prompt grid B (4 plates): four environmental negative-space variants — the same mascot poses but the shadow is cast onto a faint geometric surface (disco floor grid, frosted glass, rough paper, water) rendered at 10% o
proposals.texture: One material only: the shadow. Procedural soft-box shadow with 4px penumbra, physically calibrated to a single 45-degree light source. On scroll past 60% of invite height, the WebGL layer reveals a foil shimmer confined strictly to the mascot's goggle patches and gem — nowhere else. The foil is not decoration; it is the mascots telling you where to look. No particle systems. No bokeh on this direction. No candle flicker unless the scenario is the candle-blow plate, in which case a single flame particle — 6 frames, looped — sits at the wick tip only.
proposals.motion: Three states, in order. State 1 — load: mascot drifts from 4px below final position to rest over 400ms, ease-out cubic, no bounce. The void arrives before the mascot. State 2 — idle: phone tilt via gyroscope shifts the mascot layer ±6px on x-axis only; the shadow shifts ±3px in the opposite direction, maintaining the single light-source fiction. The void does not move. State 3 — tap the hairline circle: the mascot performs one scenario-specific micro-action (candle extinguishes, balloon string releases upward off-screen, camera shutter blinks the goggle patch), and the party detail text cross-fades from weight 300 to weight 700 — the information becomes the event. Total animation budget: nothing that lasts longer than 600ms. Reduced motion: all motion suppressed; the foil shimmer on the goggle patches is the only feedback, triggered by tap alone.
proposals.productionMethod: Two Magnific prompt grids. Grid A prompt: 'Chora and Reello kaiju characters — wide mochi head, white face, chevron cap with navy gem, purple and orange goggle patches respectively, angular magenta-orange ruff, cat-ear horns — rendered in clean 3D on pure white field, single 45-degree directional light from upper left, one soft cast shadow, eight distinct single-action poses (list poses), no background, no props except what the action requires, studio product render quality, character on-model.' Grid B prompt: same character brief, four poses, shadow cast onto [disco floor grid / frosted glass / rough paper / still water] at low opacity, otherwise identical lighting and field. All plates returned as PNG with transparency. Foreground cut-outs are extracted from the art plate and placed on a separate Tela layer. The shadow is re-rendered as a procedural shader in the WebGL layer so it resp
proposals.humanTrace: The single directional light is a decision, not a default. Every plate is editorially selected from the Magnific grid — I am choosing which shadow angle, which pose crop, which moment of the action is held. The hairline tap-target circle is drawn by hand in vector at 1px stroke before being placed — its imprecision at that scale is the only gestural mark in the design. The mascot's 8px left-of-axis placement is a specific compositional choice that leaves an intentional column of silence; that column is the editorial act.
proposals.risk: The risk is that parents and children read emptiness as unfinished — that the void feels like a failed load rather than a held breath. This risk is worth taking because Plajah's mascots are strong enough characters to hold a frame alone; the void is not absence of care, it is proof that we trusted the characters to carry the weight without scaffolding. If the foil on the goggle patches lands correctly, the child's first tap will feel like discovering something hidden in plain sight — which is the emotional logic of the whole direction.

arguesWith.why: The Dramatist will load the void with confetti, string lights, and a second light source to make the scene 'alive.' I am saying the scene is already alive — the mascot is in it. Every confetti particle The Dramatist adds is a vote of no confidence in Chora and Reello. The child should look at the monster, not around it.

disputes.objection: The state-machine proposal mistakes behavioral complexity for compositional structure: four mascot states, four depth planes, four input triggers, and a particle rate proportional to tilt magnitude accumulate into a system that cannot be read the same way twice — and a thing that cannot be read the same way twice has no measure, only behavior. The 12-column grid is invoked as governing order, but when the mascot bodies become live input-output nodes whose pose is a function of tap count and ambient light, the grid is no longer a cantus firmus organizing the whole; it is a stage that the physics engine ignores whenever the physics engine decides to. That does not resolve.
disputes.concession: The decision to lock the WebGL foil highlight vector and the Blender mascot render to a single, editorially specified light-source azimuth is exactly correct — it is a governing constraint that enforces unified light grammar across substrates, and I have said as much in my own notes; that one act of

disputes.objection: The shadow is doing all the material work and then the design calls it a texture — but one procedural soft-box shadow locked to a 45-degree preset is a default, not a decision; it has the same relationship to risk that a clean white gallery wall has to a print run. The hairline circle 'drawn by hand in vector' is the only gestural claim and it evaporates the moment it hits a retina screen — that is not leaving evidence in, that is leaving evidence out and calling the absence a philosophy. Minimalism that cannot be photocopied four times and still argue with you has not risked anything; it has just gotten quiet.
disputes.concession: The 8px left-of-axis placement creating an intentional column of negative space for the QR and link preview is a real compositional decision — it solves a functional problem structurally instead of decorating over it, and I respect that.

disputes.objection: The reveal sequence is a behaviour but it is not a system — it is a fixed cinematic script that plays the same way regardless of input, which makes it a screensaver with a schedule, not a responsive instrument. The proscenium vignette, the black hold, the curtain-rise — these are narrative conventions borrowed from theatre and re-skinned in WebGL, and none of them change state based on what the user does, what the event data says, or what the environment reports; the 'behaviour' is just a timeline. When the tap-interaction makes the mascot 'break the fourth wall' it is decorating surprise rather than building a rule for surprise, and I cannot find a governing parameter anywhere in this direc
disputes.concession: The 0.8-second candle-flicker cycle instead of 1.0 is a real performance decision — that 200ms choice is the kind of calibrated timing judgment that separates a system that feels alive from one that feels clocked, and I would carry that discipline into any direction on this table.

disputes.objection: The Minimalist calls the white void 'universal silence' but silence is not neutral — it is already a cultural proposition, one that carries the long history of Modernist reduction, which has its own geography and its own exclusions. The 8px left-of-axis placement and the hairline circle are named as editorial acts, and I accept that they are choices, but they are choices made inside a single inherited aesthetic tradition that the proposal does not name or interrogate. Specificity is not the enemy of restraint; but restraint that refuses to locate itself is just another form of unmarked universalism dressed in negative space.
disputes.concession: The shadow as the sole texture is genuinely disciplined — one physically-plausible cast shadow doing all the environmental work is the kind of constraint that forces material honesty, and I would argue for that rule in any direction I brought to this table.

disputes.objection: The hairline circle tap-target is not a reveal — it is a withholding that calls itself a reveal; hiding the party detail in negative space and making the guest hunt for it through a 32-pixel ring treats the emotion of being invited as a riddle to solve rather than a feeling to receive, and a child's birthday deserves better than a held breath that never exhales. The single shadow as the only texture is not a decision about what the work feels like — it is a decision to feel nothing until the user earns it, which is exactly the alibi restraint becomes when it stops serving the work and starts serving the designer's discomfort with commitment. Scale must match emotion: this is a kaiju, a creat
disputes.concession: The 8-pixel left-of-axis placement is genuinely right — that small asymmetry creates the column of silence that gives the negative space its pressure, and I would steal it without hesitation for a composition where the rest of the stage was actually alive.

disputes.objection: The reveal sequence is a sequence of effects pretending to be structure — black hold, fade, rise, ignite, idle, burst: six gestures where one contrast would do more. The proscenium vignette, the film grain, the volumetric haze, the foil ruffs, the candle flicker, the particle drift: none of these are editing each other, they are simply coexisting, and coexistence is not composition. When everything is dramatic, the word loses its load-bearing function.
disputes.concession: The 0.4-second black hold is a real decision — silence before sound, not decoration before content — and that instinct is structurally correct even if everything that follows undoes it.

synthesis.direction: Twelve evites built as miniature theatre: a 9×16 portrait stage with three depth planes — raked background plate, mascot mid-stage cut-out, proscenium WebGL vignette — each scene lit by a single motivated light source whose azimuth is specified by the art director before the Magnific prompt is written and locked into every downstream layer (foil shader, Blender mascot render, shadow). The reveal sequence plays on open (400ms black hold, background fades center-out over 600ms, mascot rises from below the proscenium lip, WebGL ignites in a 300ms burst then settles), with the mascot placed 8px left of center axis to open a column of negative space on the right for QR and link preview. Type is Fraunces Display 800 italic for headline, DM Sans 400 for details; both are live Tela text, never baked. Two Magnific grid runs (Birthday Opera, then eight remaining scenarios) return up to 16 plates each; editorial selection advances 12 plus alternates. The four-state mascot interaction (IDLE → ALERT → REACT → CELEBRATE) from the Futurist's state machine governs all tap and tilt response, replacing the Baroque's fixed timeline punch with a graduated rule that changes with input.
synthesis.keepFromCounterpoint: The 8px left-of-axis mascot placement that opens an intentional column of negative space — it solves the QR and link-preview problem structurally rather than decorating over it, and it gives the proscenium stage the asymmetric pressure it needs to feel composed rather than centered.
synthesis.editorCut: The Futurist removed the ambient-light sensor read and the four-depth parallax z-stack (0.0 / 0.4 / 0.8 / 1.2 rem per degree). Both add engineering surface area with marginal perceptual return on a fast-scroll mobile open; the motivated light-source lock and the three-state tilt response (gyro ±12px on mid-stage layer only, shadow shifts opposite at half magnitude) deliver the dimensional coherence without the load risk.
synthesis.openDecision: Do you want the reveal sequence to play automatically on every open — including repeat visits — or should it play once per session and resolve to a static idle state on return? This changes whether the theatre curtain is a greeting or a permanent feature of the room.
synthesis.ariaSummary:
The team agreed on one thing before anything else: the motivated light source must be a human editorial decision made before the prompt is written, not something left to the model. Every direction on the table built from that. The split was about what to do with the stage once the light was set.

I brought Baroque as lead because the brief asks for jaw-dropping and brand-building in the same breath — and the curtain-rise sequence, the chiaroscuro depth, the moment a kaiju breaks the picture plane toward a child's finger, is the only direction on the table that earns both at once. The Minimalist pushed back hard, and one thing they said is staying: the 8px left-of-axis placement that opens a column of negative space for the QR and link preview. That is a real compositional decision that solves a real problem, and I took it.

The Futurist was the editor, and they cut two things I agreed to cut: the ambient-light sensor and the four-depth parallax stack. Both were engineering cost for perceptual margin. What the Futurist kept is the four-state mascot logic — IDLE, ALERT, REACT, CELEBRATE — which replaces the Baroque's fixed timeline tap-punch with a graduated rule that actually changes with what the child does. That is the difference between a screensaver and a character.

The team disagreed sharpest on the reveal sequence itself. The Minimalist called it 'six gestures where one contrast would do more.' I took the Baroque's side: an invitation is a promise of how the party will feel, and the 400ms black hold before the curtain rises is not indulgence — it is the breath before the downbeat. The one decision I cannot make for you is whether that curtain rises every time, or only the first.
